text.insert: The Decomp Loop turns a game's open targets into validated code improvements. The harness builds a baseline, seeds an epoch queue, and runs isolated workers. Each worker submits improvements through the quality gate. The host integrates selected results into the harness worktree, then settles the epoch and runs Sync before admitting more work.
The implementation calls this workflow
Run
. Harness State records its durable progress. Dispatch State controls the lease that permits it to run.
One Epoch

steps.text: Read a fresh baseline report and collect eligible open function and section targets.
Admit targets once for the epoch, subject to the configured target cap. Worker capacity controls concurrent claims.
Capture the current committed head, provision a sandbox, and prepare the worker's task and knowledge context.
Validate each submission. Return failures for repair and retain passing improvements as selectable checkpoints.
Apply selected results one at a time to the harness worktree and commit accepted changes.
Preserve evidence for every closed worker and queue enabled knowledge processing.
Wait for worker and integration work to settle, record epoch evidence, and reconcile upstream through Sync.
Record displaced work, refresh report and knowledge, and write post-sync evidence before the next epoch.

text.insert: Ownership and Evidence

The host owns queue admission, validation, integration, and boundary decisions. Each worker owns only its claimed task and approved write set. This map connects the stages to the records they produce.
How Targets Enter the Queue

The current report supplies imperfect functions and scored non-code sections. The scheduler considers all eligible candidates unless an epoch target cap is configured. Membership stays fixed after admission; availability and missing job coverage can change as the epoch runs. Code-graph context helps workers investigate targets, but does not rank the queue.

A paused harness can prepare epoch membership after all readiness gates pass. Preparation reads the selected game's configured report and vendor exclusions, records epoch_prepared, and leaves execution paused with no dispatch lease or worker claims. Before the first activation, the operator can save worker count, timeout, model, provider, thinking level, and sandbox profile. Saving checks the Run revision, updates its policy revision and prepared worker capacity, and preserves target membership. Settings become immutable at activation. A later explicit Run request admits the prepared epoch under normal readiness, sandbox profile, and lease checks.
How Improvements Reach Other Workers

A claim captures one source commit for the worker's entire attempt. Successful integration advances the committed harness head for later claims. Existing sandboxes keep their captured base, so integration must handle changes made since a worker started. Images do not need rebuilding for each epoch.

Worker evidence and code follow separate paths. Code enters the harness worktree through Worker Result Integration. Closed worker evidence enters the knowledge base through enabled summary and librarian lanes. At the boundary, Sync refreshes external sources and code subjects and queues librarian work. Librarian completion is asynchronous.
Run State
explains identity, controls, claims, and recovery.
Worker Attempt
covers the quality gate, write safety, and sandbox lifecycle.
Worker Result Integration
explains how selected code reaches the current epoch.
Epoch Boundary
covers settlement, upstream changes, reports, and resume.
